title: Traumatic brain injury and concussion in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the head injury (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Fall from ladder, head trauma.

Vitals:
T: 98.4 F, HR: 72, RR: 16, BP: 128/78, SpO2: 97% on RA.

Recent Labs:
WBC: 8.2, Hgb: 13.1, Plt: 210, Na: 138, K: 4.0, Cr: 1.1, eGFR: 65.

Review of Systems:
Neuro: Pt c/o mild confusion and headache. No focal deficits.
CV: No chest pain, no SOB.
Resp: No cough.
GI: No N/V.
MSK: Mild neck pain.

Social History: Retired, lives with daughter. Non-smoker.

Family History: Hypertension, Type 2 DM.

Hospital Course:
80 y/o female pt admitted after fall from a ladder. Pt was unconscious for about 10 minutes at the scene. Initial neuro exam showed mild disorientation. MRI of the head revealed a diffuse brain injury. Pt was monitored closely for neurological changes. Managed with IV fluids and neuro checks q2h. Pt remained stable throughout admission. No acute changes in mentation. Transitioned to oral intake on 05/15. Pt mobile with assist.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Diffuse traumatic brain injury.

Discharge Medications:
Acetaminophen 650mg BID PRN for pain.
Multivitamin daily.

Follow-up:
F/u with Neurology in 1 week. F/u with PCP in 2 weeks.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, MD, 05/18/2026
explanations: Diffuse traumatic brain injury with loss of consciousness of 30 minutes or less, initial encounter: S06.2X1A (HCC 398).

distractors.why: There was a brief loss of consciousness.

hccs.label: Major Head Injury with Loss of Consciousness < 1 Hour or Unspecified
